text.p: Italian debt future rebounded from earlier losses following a fall in the U.S. NAPM index which prompted a rise in T-bonds, while BTPs were also supported by the bounce back in the lira, dealers said.

The U.S. National Association of Purchasing Managers index, which is viewed as a key indicator of economic performance, fell to 51.7 percent in September from 52.6 in August showing the U.S. economy was not as strong as economists had forecast.
The market was also watching the Franco-Italian row on Italy entering the European single currency, but traders said the split appeared to have been patched over.

The row was prompted after French President Jacque Chirac said he doubted that Italy would make it to be amongst the first European nations to join a European single currency, but later he appear to backtrack and say Italy would make it.
This came after Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi critised Chirac over his comments.
The Italian bond market had started lower earlier on profit-taking and a weaker lira, but the U.S. data and the T-bond rally with bunds in their wake swepted all those worries away, dealers said.
The bond market's next focus will be on key September data on U.S. non-farm payrolls on Friday, dealers said.

They added that last Friday's anouncement of a larger than expected 62.5 trillion lire 1997 financial budget to see Italy into the first group of members of the single European currency was still giving underlying support, but interest was now on would the measures really work and bring in the deficit without pushing Italy into recession.
